_about: Example for qualify_windows_battery.py. Copy it outside the repository, replace every <...> with a local path, and keep private inputs (extracted title, checkpoints, captures, references) outside the checkout. Keys starting with an underscore are comments.

build_trees.name: host
build_command: <script that sets up the compiler and runs ninja -C the host tree>

test_env._about: Tests needing ROM-derived inputs read them from here and report themselves skipped (77) without them.

build_trees.name: gpu
build_command: <script that runs ninja -C the GPU test tree>

scenarios._about: L5. Each item runs once per output size as TriAevum.exe (hard links) in the working directory, a Forge installation. Captures, the runtime report and per-frame renderer diagnostics (gpu.json) stay in the report directory. 'references' holds accepted captures per item and size; a missing reference is reported as not run.
scenarios._expect: exit, captures (count), reference (byte identity), full_width_desaturation (captures whose every column is grey), black_bars (captures whose pixels outside the fitted picture of 'picture_native' proportions, default 400x240, are black), and bounds on per-frame renderer counters: <counter>_max for every frame, <counter>_min_total for the run, with counter one of screen_content, whole_target_ui, own_picture, picture_bars, picture_overlay, dlss_upscale, native_ui_overlay. qualify_windows_battery.py --scenarios NAME,... runs only the named items.
scenarios.config: <settings JSON used when an item names none>
scenarios.save_data_seed: <save data directory copied for every run>
scenarios.gpu_lock: <optional lock directory shared with other GPU jobs>
